headline: Walmart beat on revenue and EPS and raised its sales outlook, but U.S. comps slowed to 2.6% and shares fell ~9%.
guidance_note: FY27 net sales growth raised to 4-5% (from 3.5-4.5%), adj. EPS $2.80-2.87; Q3 guide of 3-3.75% sales and $0.62-0.64 EPS disappointed.
key_messages: Walmart U.S. comp ex fuel slowed to +2.6% (transactions +1.5%, ticket +1.1%) vs ~3.5-3.8% expected; pharmacy drug-pricing law cut ~125 bps.
Sam's Club U.S. comp ex fuel +4.4% with transactions up ~7%; Sam's eCommerce +26%.
Global eCommerce +23%, Walmart U.S. eCommerce +24%; U.S. marketplace sales +52%.
Tariff (IEEPA) refunds lifted gross margin; Walmart is plowing them into prices (>11,000 rollbacks vs 7,200 at end of Q1).
Fuel costs expected to exceed $2B for the year; Walmart U.S. inventory up ~6.3% partly on cost inflation.

consumer.income_split: Share gains across the business; lower-income households managing trade-offs as fuel prices rose. CFO John David Rainey said higher fuel prices prompted more trade-offs, particularly in June.
consumer.pricing: Tariff refunds reinvested into rollbacks, especially consumables; cost inflation and higher fuel costs noted.

macro_read: Even the share-gaining value leader saw U.S. comps decelerate as fuel costs squeezed budgets, pointing to a consumer making more trade-offs mid-2026.
